current.kana: こんばんわかれーをつくる

structure_explanation.en: Note: the parser merged 今晩は as if it were the greeting こんばんは ('good evening'), but in context it is 今晩 (こんばん, this evening) + は (topic particle) = 'as for tonight'. カレー (curry) is the object, marked by を, and 作る (つくる, to make/prepare) is the verb. The focus is the vocabulary 晩 (evening) within 今晩.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Atenção: o analisador juntou 今晩は como se fosse a saudação こんばんは ('boa noite'), mas no contexto é 今晩 (こんばん, esta noite) + は (partícula de tópico) = 'falando de hoje à noite'. カレー (curry) é o objeto, marcado por を, e 作る (つくる, fazer/preparar) é o verbo. O foco é o vocabulário 晩 (noite) dentro de 今晩.

translation_literal.en: As for tonight, I'll make curry.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a esta noite, curry faço.

translation.en: Tonight I'm going to make curry.
translation.pt-BR: Hoje à noite vou fazer curry.

note.en: the correct reading in context is 今晩(こんばん)+は, not the greeting こんばんは
note.pt-BR: leitura correta no contexto é 今晩(こんばん)+は, não a saudação こんばんは
forma de dicionário (plain) de 作る

objections.objection: Corpus-build tooling is exposed in learner-facing prose: 'the parser merged 今晩は as if it were the greeting こんばんは' / 'o analisador juntou 今晩は como se fosse a saudação こんばんは'. This is the exact defect class the same batch identifies and fixes in sent:gen-bff5315e9c4b (op: "Learner-facing explanation leaks internal tooling ('the parser tagged 様 as さま/noun')"), where the wording was rewritten to plain pedagogy. Shipping the fix in one record and leaving the identical leak in another leaves the corpus internally inconsistent; the point can be made without naming the parser. The reading fix itself (こんばんは→こんばんわ, konbanha→konbanwa) is correct.
objections.auditor_hint: en: 'Careful: 今晩は here is not the greeting こんばんは (good evening); it is 今晩 (こんばん, this evening) + は (topic particle) = as for tonight, so it is read こんばんわ. カレー (curry) is the object, marked by を, and 作る (つくる, to make/prepare) is the verb. The focus is the vocabulary 晩 (evening) within 今晩.' / pt-BR: 'Atenção: 今晩は aqui não é a saudação こんばんは (boa noite); é 今晩 (こんばん, esta noite) + は (partícula de tópico) = falando de hoje à noite, por isso se lê こんばんわ. カレー (curry) é o objeto, marcado por を, e 作る (つくる, fazer/preparar) é o verbo. O foco é o vocabulário 晩 (noite) dentro de 今晩.'

current.jp: 財布にお金がありません
current.kana: さいふにおかねがありません

structure_explanation.en: Existence sentence in the negative. 財布に indicates the place ('in the wallet') with the particle に, お金 ('money') is the subject marked by が, and the verb ある ('to exist/there is', for inanimate things) appears negated and polite as ありません. In pt-BR, 'haver/existir dinheiro' naturally becomes 'ter dinheiro', hence 'não tem dinheiro na carteira'.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Frase de existência no negativo. 財布に indica o local ('na carteira') com a partícula に, お金 ('dinheiro') é o sujeito marcado por が, e o verbo ある ('existir/haver', para coisas inanimadas) aparece negado e polido como ありません. Em pt-BR, 'haver/existir dinheiro' soa naturalmente como 'ter dinheiro', por isso 'não tem dinheiro na carteira'.

translation_literal.en: In the wallet, there is no money.

translation.en: There's no money in the wallet.

note.en: stem of ある, base for the polite negative ありません
note.pt-BR: radical de ある, base para a negação polida ありません

note.en: ます in negative form ませ
note.pt-BR: ます em forma negativa ませ

note.en: ん completes the polite negation; ませ + ん = ません
note.pt-BR: ん completa a negação polida; ませ+ん = ません

objections.objection: The fix removes an illogical English claim but replaces it with a pt-BR-specific note inside the English locale field: "In pt-BR, 'haver/existir dinheiro' naturally becomes 'ter dinheiro', hence 'nao tem dinheiro na carteira'." The en explanation now ends in Portuguese and explains a Portuguese translation choice to an English reader. This breaks the convention the batch itself follows (cf. sent:gen-cc5475411409, where en says "In English the koto is not translated literally" while pt-BR says "Em pt-BR o koto nao se traduz literalmente") - each locale comments on its own language. The correct fix is to drop the clause from en (English 'there is no money' needs no such note), keeping the pt-BR note where it belongs.
objections.auditor_hint: Existence sentence in the negative. 財布に indicates the place ('in the wallet') with the particle に, お金 ('money') is the subject marked by が, and the verb ある ('to exist/there is', for inanimate things) appears negated and polite as ありません.

current.jp: 海にサンダルで行った
current.kana: うみにさんだるでいった

structure_explanation.en: 海に marks the destination of the movement (に of direction), and サンダルで uses で in the sense of 'state/manner' (going 'in sandals', wearing sandals). The verb 行った is the past of 行く (いく, 'to go'), read いった. Careful: the same kanji 行 also writes 行う (おこなう, 'to carry out'), whose past is 行った read おこなった — here the destination + means context makes it 行く.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: 海に marca o destino do deslocamento (に de direção), e サンダルで usa で no sentido de 'estado/modo' (indo 'de sandália', calçando sandália). O verbo 行った é o passado de 行く (いく, 'ir'), lido いった. Atenção: o mesmo kanji 行 também escreve 行う (おこなう, 'realizar'), cujo passado 行った se lê おこなった — aqui, pelo contexto de destino + meio, o verbo é 行く.

translation_literal.en: I went to the sea in sandals.

translation.en: I went to the beach in sandals.

note.en: past form of 行く: 行った (not 行う 'to carry out', despite the analyzer's label)
note.pt-BR: forma passada de 行く: 行った (não 行う 'realizar', apesar do rótulo do analisador)

objections.objection: Same tooling leak at token level: the note still ends '(not 行う to carry out, despite the analyzer's label)' / '(não 行う realizar, apesar do rótulo do analisador)'. 'The analyzer' / 'o analisador' is corpus-build metadata in learner-facing text and is now dangling, since the token reading it contradicts was changed to いっ by this very patch.
objections.auditor_hint: en: "past form of 行く: 行った (いった) — not 行う 'to carry out'" / pt-BR: "forma passada de 行く: 行った (いった) — não 行う 'realizar'"

current.jp: ビールが温くなってしまった
current.kana: びーるがぬるくなってしまった

structure_explanation.en: The sentence combines two patterns. First 温く + なる: the い-adjective 温い shifts to the adverbial form 温く and links to なる to indicate a CHANGE of state ('to get lukewarm'). Then なる appears in the て-form (なって) + しまう, the pattern 〜てしまう, which here marks an undesirable/regrettable result ('to end up ~'), all in the past with 〜た. That is, the beer, which should have been cold, ended up lukewarm, which is bad.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase combina dois padrões. Primeiro 温く + なる: o adjetivo-i 温い passa para a forma adverbial 温く e se liga a なる para indicar MUDANÇA de estado ('ficar morno'). Depois なる aparece na forma-て (なって) + しまう, padrão 〜てしまう, que aqui marca um resultado indesejado/lamentável ('acabar ~'), tudo no passado com 〜た. Ou seja, a cerveja, que devia estar gelada, ficou morna, o que é ruim.

translation_literal.en: As for the beer, it went warm on me.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto à cerveja, ficou morna e acabou (terminou indesejavelmente).

translation.en: The beer ended up getting warm (it lost its chill).
translation.pt-BR: A cerveja acabou esquentando (perdeu o gelado).

note.en: adverbial form 温く of 温い (i-adjective, い changes to く) to link to なる
note.pt-BR: forma adverbial 温く de 温い (adjetivo-i, troca い por く) para ligar a なる

note.en: te-form なって (of なる) to connect to しまう
note.pt-BR: forma-て なって (de なる) para conectar a しまう

note.en: しまう in the past form しまった (なってしまった)
note.pt-BR: しまう na forma passada しまった (なってしまった)

objections.objection: ビール is marked by が, yet the literal mirrors still read 'As for the beer, it went warm on me.' / 'Quanto à cerveja, ficou morna e acabou (terminou indesejavelmente).' This batch explicitly rules that the 'As for X / Quanto a X' device mirrors は only, and applies exactly that fix to five sibling records here (e5a12e393735, e5c28d30ded1, e619592cd255, e6f956627466, eaaae06d8210 — all が/を cases). Shipping this record unrepaired leaves a topic construction on a が-marked subject and makes the batch inconsistent with the rule it just enforced elsewhere.
objections.auditor_hint: en: 'The beer (が) ended up going warm.' / pt-BR: 'A cerveja (が) ficou morna e acabou (terminou indesejavelmente).'

structure_explanation.en: ...marked by が as that which (does not) exist, the adverb もう (with a negative: 'no more / not anymore') and the adjective ない...
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase usa o padrão de existência: マッチ (fósforo) marcado por が como o que (não) existe, o advérbio もう (já) e o adjetivo ない (não existir/não ter), que é a forma negativa do verbo de existência ある para coisas inanimadas. O foco de vocabulário é マッチ (fósforo). Note que aqui ない funciona como a negação de 'haver/ter', resultando em 'já não tem mais'.

translation_literal.en: As for matches, (subject) there are no longer any.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a fósforo, (sujeito) já não existe.

gloss.en: to not have / to not exist

note.en: negative form corresponding to ある (to exist, for inanimates)
note.pt-BR: forma negativa correspondente a ある (existir, para inanimados)

objections.objection: マッチ is marked by が, but the literal mirrors keep the は device: 'As for matches, (subject) there are no longer any.' / 'Quanto a fósforo, (sujeito) já não existe.' Worse, each string is self-contradictory — it applies the topic device and then explicitly labels the same constituent '(subject)/(sujeito)'. Same rule and same fix pattern as the five records repaired in this batch; leaving it blurs は vs が for learners in both locales.
